items.summary: An open-source (AGPL-3.0) Android app that runs DeepSeek's open-source agent engine, DeepSeek Harness, on the phone itself: it bundles Ubuntu 24.04 and Node.js 24 inside the app via proot, with no root or Termux needed. With accessibility permission it can read the screen, tap and type to operate the phone; it can also remote-control a DSH instance on a PC or server over SSH or the end-to-end encrypted DSH Remote relay. Released Oct 25, it passed 6,000 stars in about a week.
items.title: DSH Go: DeepSeek Harness in your pocket — run the agent on the phone or remote-control the one on your computer (AGPL, GitHub trending Nov 5)

items.summary: A hosted MCP server at https://mcp.phone-harness.com/mcp. Any MCP-compatible agent — Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and more — pastes the URL, signs in, and gets 15 tools to read the screen, tap, type and swipe on a real cloud iPhone or Android emulator. The local version drives your own phone instead: iPhone via the Mac's iPhone Mirroring window, Android over adb, with no jailbreak or root. The open-source harness is MIT licensed; cloud Android bills at 5 cents a phone-minute with $5 of trial credit.
items.title: Phone Harness MCP: paste one URL and any MCP agent can drive a real cloud iPhone or Android (launched Nov 2)

items.summary: A hands-on write-up: a laptop connects over Tailscale to Tailscale Aperture, an AI gateway that authenticates and routes by model name; llama-swap starts a vLLM child process on demand and kills it after about 5 idle minutes to free VRAM, with vLLM serving Qwen3.6 27B. No open ports and no reverse proxy to maintain — a setup pattern that transfers directly to a home GPU box.
items.title: Self-hosted local LLM server in practice: Tailscale gateway plus on-demand model loading, zero open ports (Hacker News, Nov 4)
